speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (C5-C6) with associated muscle wasting due to chronic compression.

I have noted your history of heavy lifting, steroid use, and weight loss, which can mimic these symptoms, but the progressive weakness and dropping objects require immediate evaluation. Given your history of diabetes and alcohol use, we must also rule out neuropathy; however, the focal nature of the arm weakness points strongly to a spinal issue. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cervical_Spine to visualize the spinal cord compression.
